subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In the early 1970s, the US had strict regulations limiting women's participation in college athletics.
• The amount of funding for women's sports programs was typically less than 2% of total athletic budgets.
• This system heavily favored men's sports programs.
• Nearly 90% of athletic scholarships were awarded to male athletes.
• The 1972 Title IX Education Amendments prohibited sex-based discrimination in education programs.
prompt: The student wants to present the significance of Title IX to an audience unfamiliar with the history of women's athletics. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Nearly 90% of athletic scholarships were awarded to male athletes at the time Title IX was proposed.
choices.B: Prior to Title IX, women's sports programs typically received less than 2% of total athletic budgets.
choices.C: The 1972 Title IX Education Amendments prohibited sex-based discrimination in education programs, which had heavily favored men's sports.
choices.D: The regulations in place in the early 1970s were addressed by the 1972 Title IX Education Amendments.

explanation:
Choice C is correct. It presents Title IX's significance: the 1972 amendments prohibited sex-based discrimination, which mattered because the old system heavily favored men's sports.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. The sentence describes an aspect of athletic funding at the time Title IX was proposed; it doesn't present the significance of Title IX to an audience unfamiliar with the history of women's athletics.
